{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "For Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as the fixed factor. Given the right-skewed distribution (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81), consider log-transformation or robust ANOVA. The large sample size (n=76,655) provides power to detect small effects.",
    "For Success: Binary outcome (0/1) makes standard ANOVA inappropriate. Use logistic regression or a generalized linear model with binomial family and logit link, treating Stim Paradigm as a categorical predictor.",
    "For Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. The extreme right skew (max=29.82 vs mean=0.47) and presence of values >>1 suggests heavy-tailed distribution; consider log-transformation, rank-based ANOVA, or permutation ANOVA.",
    "For Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Distribution appears more reasonable (max=75.35, mean=12.50), though some positive skew present; standard ANOVA may suffice with outlier screening.",
    "For AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Bounded [0,1] interval with mean 0.38 suggests reasonable distribution for ANOVA, though beta regression or arcsine transformation could improve variance stabilization."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Assumes trial-level independence; violated if multiple trials per mouse are correlated. The 8 mice with highly unequal trial counts (range 7,233-10,986) suggest strong clustering—this is a critical violation requiring mixed-effects models.",
    "Normality: QQ-plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests for each Stim Paradigm group; severe expected violations for Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency due to extreme outliers.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test for equality of variances across paradigms; likely violated given dramatically different ranges across variables.",
    "For Success (binary): Standard ANOVA assumptions fundamentally violated; binomial GLM assumptions (linearity in logit, overdispersion) must be checked.",
    "For AD: Check boundary issues—values near 0 or 1 may cause heteroscedasticity in standard ANOVA."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus ANOVA is significant: Pairwise comparisons with Tukey HSD for Time-to-Target, Average Speed, and AD (or their transformed versions), controlling family-wise error rate across 10 pairwise comparisons.",
    "For Path Efficiency: Given distributional concerns, use Dunn's test (Kruskal-Wallis post-hoc) or pairwise Wilcoxon with Bonferroni correction rather than parametric Tukey.",
    "For Success: Post-hoc contrasts in logistic regression framework using Wald tests with multiplicity correction (Tukey or Bonferroni).",
    "Focus comparisons on Combined versus single-modality conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) and versus Sham to assess potential multimodal enhancement effects.",
    "Effect sizes: Report eta-squared (or partial eta-squared) for ANOVAs, odds ratios for Success, and Cliff's delta for non-parametric comparisons."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined stimulation likely shows faster Time-to-Target and higher Success than single-modality or Sham conditions based on typical multimodal enhancement literature, though this is speculative without data access.",
    "ICMS Only may differ from Visual conditions in Path Efficiency and AD, reflecting different spatial processing strategies (proprioceptive vs. visual guidance).",
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance across metrics if stimulation is effective.",
    "Dim vs. Bright Visual Only may differ in Average Speed and Time-to-Target due to visibility constraints.",
    "AD (angular dispersion) may be lowest for Combined, indicating straighter paths with multimodal guidance."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Cannot verify actual statistical significance without raw data or group-level statistics (means, SDs, n per group).",
    "Severe mouse-level clustering unaddressed: 8 mice with 7,233-10,986 trials each creates massive non-independence. Standard ANOVA results would be anti-conservative and potentially misleading.",
    "Extreme outliers in Time-to-Target (max 201.39s, ~100x median) and Path Efficiency (max 29.82) suggest possible data quality issues or rare event types that may require censoring or separate analysis.",
    "Unequal group sizes (Combined: 48,846; Sham: 3,505) reduce power for Sham comparisons and may affect ANOVA robustness.",
    "No information on trial sequence, learning effects, or block structure that could affect performance.",
    "Temperature=0.75 and prompt template effects on analysis approach are meta-analytical factors, not biological ones."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) for Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and AD, and a generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) with binomial family for Success, all with Stim Paradigm as fixed effect and Mouse as random intercept. This addresses the critical non-independence from repeated measures. Include paradigm-by-mouse random slopes if convergence permits. Compare model fit via likelihood ratio tests and report marginal means with confidence intervals. For Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target, consider gamma or log-normal GLMMs to handle skewness."
}
